title: fix(create-plugin): stop stamping an "ObjectStack Inc." copyright header on the author's own source
body:
Fixes #8778

The scaffolder opened every source file it wrote for the plugin author with this project's copyright claim. That claim is gone. Nothing replaces it.

## What was ruled, and what stays fenced

Triage ruled the REMOVAL and explicitly fenced the REPLACEMENT: any substitute is a legal assertion about the author's code. This PR takes the safe landing named there — emit no copyright header, because that asserts nothing. **No substitute was chosen, and no maintainer question is being answered here.**

## The emitters — enumerated, not assumed

The brief assumed exactly four. Confirmed, and they are the only four:

| builder | emits |
| --- | --- |
| `buildIndexFile` | `src/index.tsx` |
| `buildImplFile` | the component implementation |
| `buildTypesFile` | `src/types.ts` |
| `buildTestFile` | the example test |

All four live in `packages/create-plugin/src/templates.ts` and are contiguous. A whole-repo sweep for the interpolated form found no fifth emitter and no variant: the only other `Copyright` strings this package produces are the licence TEXTS in `src/licenses.ts`, whose holder is the author (`licenseCopyrightHolder`) — objectui#8041 / objectui#8892 territory, and correct. The three literal headers in `templates.ts`, `licenses.ts` and `index.ts` are this repo's OWN source and are untouched.

## Was the rest of the block true? Yes — and that decided the shape of the fix

The brief asked me to check whether the copyright line was the only remaining false statement, because a second one would change the trade-off. There is no second one, and the block's remaining sentence is not merely true, it is load-bearing:

- the LICENSE it points at really is emitted, by `buildPluginFiles`, beside those four files;
- the licence it names is the one the author chose at the prompt (objectui#8041);
- `buildLicenseFile` refuses an id it has no text for (objectui#8892), so the sentence cannot name a licence the package does not carry;
- it is one of the SIX agreeing licence statements those two cards built. For any one of these four files the other five are the manifest, the README and its three sibling headers.

⇒ **Deleting the whole block would have silently dropped four of those six**, and it reddens two landed tests that read them — `licenses.test.ts` "names one licence, not two" and the objectui#8892 six-way agreement case. So the deletion is scoped to the ownership lines. The trade-off the brief flagged is real, and it resolves this way.

## What was removed, and what was left

Removed from all four, 12 lines:

- the `Copyright (c) YEAR-present ObjectStack Inc.` line (YEAR spelled as a word — see the byte note below);
- the `ObjectUI` title line above it, because a line naming this project on the author's source is the same defect one line shorter;
- the blank comment line that separated them from the sentence below.

Left: the licence pointer, alone. A scaffolded source file now opens with exactly

```
This source code is licensed under the MIT license found in the
LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
```

wrapped in a block comment, with the id following the author's choice.

Also added: one note above the four builders recording that the absence is deliberate and that nothing may be put back without a maintainer decision. Without it the next contributor reads four headerless templates as an oversight.

## Acceptance — end to end, the way the card was measured

The built bin, through a pty, with answers, into a scratch directory; the four emitted files then read off disk. Two cases in `cli-cancel-and-nontty-8786.test.ts`, which is where they must live: a second test file building this package would clean `dist/` out from under the runs already there.

1. **the four claim ownership of nothing** — no `Copyright`, no `(c)`, no copyright sign, no `ObjectStack`, no `ObjectUI`, no `SPDX`, no `All rights reserved`, and not the author's answered name either. The author is answered as `Ada` precisely so the fenced substitution has a value it could have been made from; a blank-author run could not tell "we chose not to name the author" from "there was no author to name".
2. **they open with the licence pointer and nothing else** — the leading comment pinned verbatim against the id read back off the manifest, because "no copyright header" and "no header" are different landings and only one of them is this card's.

⚠️ Absence is the assertion that passes while witnessing nothing, so both controls are asserted: the ten-file list is pinned BEFORE any absence is read, and the same run's LICENSE is required to carry the very copyright line these four must not.

### The ablation

Prediction stated before running: exactly the 2 new cases redden; the 8 pre-existing cases in that file stay green, because they only require a `licensed under` line that the restored header still carries.

Measured, both legs with on-disk proof and a trap-guarded restore:

| leg | evidence |
| --- | --- |
| mutate | 4 sites rewritten; `grep -c` on disk = 4; blob hash changed from the HEAD blob |
| reached the artefact | rebuilt `dist/index.js` carries the marker 4 times — the bin the tests actually drive |
| run | exit 1 — **2 failed, 8 passed**, exactly as predicted, both failures naming the real emitted text |
| restore | `git checkout HEAD` on the path; blob hash back to the HEAD blob; `git diff HEAD` empty |
| re-run | exit 0, and `dist/index.js` marker count back to 0, so nothing mutated is left behind |

The reddening also settles what a passing count alone could not: those two cases really ran, and really witnessed the emitted bytes.

## Gates

| gate | exit | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type-check` (create-plugin) | 0 | both projects, incl. the test tsconfig |
| package suite, from the repo root | 0 | 3 files, 40 tests |
| `lint` (this package, as turbo runs it) | 0 | |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 | plus a manual sweep of both edited files |
| `check:changeset-presence` | 0 | patch changeset added |
| `check:governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 | NOT GOVERNED — 3 paths, 0 matched |
| `check:new-line-citations` | 0 | |
| `check:doc-snippets` | 0 | 638 of 638 blocks judged, 0 failed |
| `check:doc-types` | 0 | |
| `check:doc-examples` | 0 | 124 blocks, every failure a declared ledger row |
| census pin test | 0 | 27 tests — it is the suite that reads `templates.ts` |

`check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples` both returned **2** first. That is PREREQUISITE NOT MET, not a pass, so the scoped build they name was run (35 tasks, all successful) and both were re-run to the exits above.

**Declared narrowing — repo-wide lint.** `turbo run lint` across the whole workspace is CI's run, not this PR's. The narrowing is evidenced rather than assumed: the population is 4741 files, read from eslint's own `--format json` output rather than estimated; both files this PR touches report 0 errors and 0 warnings in that same run; and the config enables no type-aware linting (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, and no `project` key anywhere in `eslint.config.js`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. A repo-wide run does report 95 pre-existing errors, none of them in this diff.

## Serial adjacency — re-derived, not quoted

Re-derived against live open PRs rather than from the brief's snapshot, which had gone stale: **no currently-open PR touches `packages/create-plugin/`** (checked file-by-file across all 8). The two PRs the brief listed as in the merge queue had both already merged, and `origin/main` has since advanced past this branch's base by those two commits — neither touches this package, so there is no overlap to reconcile.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while here, **not** filed and **not** changed:

- `buildReadme` writes its `## License` line as the id, a copyright sign and `vars.author` raw, while the LICENSE goes through `licenseCopyrightHolder`. On a blank author the README line trails off after the copyright sign where the LICENSE says "the PACKAGE authors". Untouched: a licence-text question, and the objectui#8041 dispatch held every emitted file constant. Carrier: whoever next opens the licence-text half of this file.
- `packageName` is hard-coded to this project's npm scope, so a scaffolded plugin is named in a scope its author does not own. Out of scope for a copyright-header card, and a product call rather than a defect. Carrier: none today.

## A note on how this body is written

Placeholders are spelled as capitalised words rather than in the bracket shape, because this repo has measured that the shape is deleted from stored bodies even inside backticks and fenced blocks. Only objectui#8778 is written with a closing keyword; every other card is referenced bare.
